correctness.rationale: Two singular outputs are attained with C=0; otherwise exchange the outputs if necessary and normalize the invertible one to I. For T=X^(-1)Y, the determinant identity for a rank-one subtraction gives v^T u=1 and v^T Tu=tr(T)-det(T). If T is nonscalar, some u makes (u,Tu) a basis: invariance of the two basis lines and their sum line would force the same scalar on both basis vectors. Prescribe the two evaluations of the linear form on that basis. If T=lambda I, the first equation forces tr(C')=1 and the other determinant is lambda(lambda-1); for either allowed lambda=0,1 an elementary rank-one projector works. No field-size or characteristic assumption is needed. The exceptional set is the open subset of the rank-one 4-by-2 cone given by invertible X and Y neither zero nor X. Its scalar parameter is recovered regularly wherever X is invertible. The irreducible cone has 5-dimensional smooth pivot charts off the origin, full 8-dimensional tangent space at the vertex, and Segre degree binom(4,1)=4. Off the cone the image contains a dense open; rational density follows over infinite fields and geometric density follows on base change. Counting independent columns gives the stated finite-field count. An independent full-complement enumeration over F2, F3 and F4 gave (attained, missing)=(256,0),(6513,48),(65176,360).
